steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Pascuala! You made it. Here I was, thinking you were buried in the Flat.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: *Huff*...

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: You're as pale as the salt. Run into something on the way?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Shut up, Teach... Let me in already.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: You wanna come in? Did you get what the boss asked for?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: 'Course I did. Not just the compass, either. I got another big haul too.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Señora Juana's been looking for an alchemist, and I've got a lead.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: So can I come in now?

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Of course, Master Thief Pascuala. You honor my humble abode.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Anchors aweigh, hoist the sails♪

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: High winds roar, our clothes a-tore♪

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Rain drowns our drunken haze, and lights our hearts ablaze♪

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Ready, ho! Sail forth! A thousand ships break port!♪

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: At dawn break we charge ahead♪...

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Aaaahhhh! Who are you?! What're you doing in my house?!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: This alley... is your house, señor?

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: That cardboard you've got on your head is my bed, joven...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Sorry, I saw it by the garbage bin. Didn't think anyone wanted it.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Mind if I hide from the rain here? I'll go once it stops.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: This town hasn't seen a drop in over two months.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Even if it is going to rain, mind putting down my bed? Here, you can use my blanket.

spans.text: going to rain, mind putting down my bed? Here, you can use my blanket.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Thank you, señor.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: So what're you here for, Ægir?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm looking for a local sword technique. The legends say the ones who devised it were—

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ahem. A few months ago, I heard about a technique that can 'fight the wind and waves', and decided to come here to learn it.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: That's mighty brave of you. Don't you know the Inquisition's been cracking down on pirates these days?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I'm not interested in becoming a pirate. I just feel like my own swordsmanship's been lacking.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Swords are for cutting people down, not cutting through the waves. Besides, why'd you want to learn it anyway? Heading out to sea?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Too many questions, señor.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: *Sigh* There's always folks believing such foolishness. If you'd come by half a year earlier, I could have brought you to the guy you're looking for.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: Back in the day, he learned a thing or two from those pirates, always bragging about how he could chop up the sea itself. In the end, he was just like me. Came running back to town, waiting to die in peace and quiet.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Did he leave anything behind?

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: His diary? Took that to his grave. You'll have to dig it up yourself.

steps.name: Tottering Old Man
steps.text: If he knew someone wanted to learn the sword from him, he'd be so happy he'd jump right out, bones and all.
With a shovel by his side, Isidro cracks open the coffin. He brushes aside the grains of salt that fell inside, exposing a lustrous, red-flushed corpse.
The corner of a book pokes out of its clothes.
Isidro gingerly pinches the book and pulls it away, doing everything he can to keep the flimsy paper—made brittle by the salt—intact.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Is this the diary he mentioned?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: It's too tattered, I can't read a thing.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: *Cough* *Cough* *Cough*... Pfft—pleh!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Did I just inhale bits of paper...? Damn, that's salty.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I should look elsewhere.
Elsewhere? Where else would a wicked grave robber and cannibal such as yourself want to spread his evil?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Grave robber? Cannibal???
I've been watching you creep about the cemetery, molesting its graves. I've caught you red-handed.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I can explain, señor.
'Señor'...? Do you not know who I am?!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Do you... happen to be a local celebrity?
I am a cleric of the Inquisition, in charge of inspecting the entry permits of all visitors at the town gates.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: So if you don't know who I am, then how did you get in here?

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Guards! Arrest this man!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Are these petals crushed enough...?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Doctor Añora!

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: What? Oh! More or less, a few more times and you can start blending in the oil.

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: Why are your hands shaking?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: You must be mistaken.

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: Taken? What was taken?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I said! You must be mistaken!!!

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: About what? What are you on about? Still, that much shaking... Have you been drinking again?

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: You're the town calificador, you shouldn't be drinking. Wine is sinful and brings only harm, you said so yourself.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I may have had a few cups with the representative of the wine caravan as we talked business, but it was all for the sake of securing the town's future.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: How is the widow doing, Doctor?

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: The who now? Speak up!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The potter's widow! She's giving birth in a few days!

steps.name: Añora
steps.text: Gaining girth? And now gluttony, yet more sin.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I said!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The widow!!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Is giving birth!!!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Señor Silver—!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Ah—! Dios mio, you scared me. Didn't I say to knock before you enter?

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: I heard you shouting and assumed you were in danger!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: I, uh, aside from that... I have something to report.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: We've captured a... a lunatic, a blasphemer in the cemetery east of town. He was stealing corpses in the cemetery.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I... I thought that with enough food, we could avoid such a tragedy happening again.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: If I may, Señor Silver, a full belly is not enough.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: When you first brought the holy Law to our town, you cleansed us of our sins. But now? Not only have your prohibitions been lifted, we have not heard your sermons in a very long time.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Sin flourishes once more. It is inescapable.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Is that what you think?

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Which is precisely why you cannot allow this vile blasphemer to spread his evil in town!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...I shall arrange a sentencing.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: What of Old Palo? He was seen talking to the blasphemer, for quite a while at that.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...No need. Palo may have associated with pirates in his youth, but he wouldn't have the nerve to break the law.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I said there is no need.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Sir... I believe we should at least keep an eye on him.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: We can discuss this later.

steps.name: Frightened Townsperson
steps.text: Digging up a grave? Don't tell me he was about to... you know...?

steps.name: Hostile Townsperson
steps.text: Sinner! A sinner! Aarón is no longer pure... Calamity comes once more...

steps.name: Hostile Townsperson
steps.text: Padre, Calificador! I beg you, kill him! Cleanse his sins! Don't let us be visited by disaster again!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Struggles)

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Stop that!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Señor Isidro, is it true you were stealing from the graves of this town's residents in the middle of the night?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I don't deny being at the cemetery, but I—
What?!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Pascuala?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Isidro, amigo, I never took you for a grave robber. Of all the things to steal, corpses? Really?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Makes me right sick, it does.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Might I remind you, Pascuala, that you're chained up too.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Silence, sinner! You'll be on trial next!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: What are you even doing here?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I... *sigh* Old habits.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: She's about to be executed?!

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Don't blame me, that girl ran afoul of her bad habits. Barely out the door and she was already off to pick the pocket of the best dressed man in town.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Who happened to be Calificador Silver.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: With her skills, not even the calificador would have noticed her.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: He didn't, but she was caught in the act by one of his priests giving a report.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: And what about that alchemist she mentioned?

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: We know where he is.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: That's good.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: He's about to be hanged, right alongside her.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: So, how many of those priests do they have at the execution?

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Twelve.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: ...With your crew, we should be able to handle them. Let's go.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Señoras y señores, according to the laws of this town, these two criminals will be hanged by the neck until dead. I hope this will serve as a warning to all not to allow your souls to be tarnished by sin.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The time has come. Execute them.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You don't look worried at all.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: What's there to worry about?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You got a way out of this then?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Not at this exact moment, no, but it's all about the timing...

spans.text: moment, no, but it's all about the timing...

steps.text: The girl turns her head, looking to the side of the gallows. A warrior priest has his hand on the lever, ready to pull it.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: (Waves his hand)

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Agh! My hand!

steps.name: Frantic Townsperson
steps.text: B—Bandits! Bandits!

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: OhwhatsinshaveIcommittedtodeservesuchpunishmenthowshouldIatone...

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Repel them! Protect the civilians! Cover Calificador Silver's retreat!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Forget me! Evacuate the citizens!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Charge, you lazy sons of saltfins, charge! Don't let those poor bastards bite the dust!

steps.name: Howling Sailor
steps.text: Yearrrgh!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Those bandits are here to rescue their friends!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Get in formation and stop them!

steps.name: Sword-Wielding Sailor
steps.text: Die!

steps.name: Impulsive Sailor
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: You dare plunder this town so brazenly?!

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: We'll handle this lot, Javier! You save Pascuala and the boy, quicklike!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I owe you one.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Don't let them have their way!

steps.name: Warrior Priests
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Keep it quick! There's no time to waste!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Anyone gets in our way, cut them down!

steps.name: Howling Sailor
steps.text: Aye!

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Grkh...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Cut them loose, quick!

steps.name: Menacing Sailor
steps.text: On it!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Heh, took you guys long enough. Quick, get me out of these shackles, it's starting to chafe like you wouldn't believe.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Yeow! My wrists! You call this a rescue?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Hmph. Like I told the boss long ago, you're nothing but trouble.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: And yet here you are, saving me from the gallows.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You too, chaval. Get moving.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Can I borrow a sword?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Here, catch.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Don't even think about running, boy!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You expect me to lay down and die, señor?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Nice moves!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Muchas gracias.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hey! Is this really the time to get all buddy-buddy?! How're we getting out of here?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Shut your mouth and follow Teach. She knows an alley leading out of town.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: An alley? I guess that'll do...

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Follow me!

steps.name: Warrior Priest A
steps.text: They're heading south!

steps.name: Warrior Priest B
steps.text: South...? It's a sheer cliff. What're they up to?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: *Huff*... *Huff*... You're nuts. What alley?! That's a CLIFF!

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: There's an alley if you jump down.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Please tell me she's joking, Javier.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Run faster! You'll need the speed to make the jump!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: (Silently speeds up)

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Don't tell me you're going along with this plan?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Any better ideas?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: I think you've got brain problems, amigo.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: It's just ahead! Three, two, one—JUMP!
With a decisive leap, the bandit jumps down the cliff, knocking loose some rocks that fall alongside her. After a long silence, a distant, muffled 'thump' can be heard coming from the bottom.
Pascuala watches bandit and boulder alike disappear off the cliff's edge, and gulps in fear.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Urk...

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: It's a dead end up ahead, there's nowhere to run! Get them!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Jump already! They're about to catch up!
Pascuala looks at the cliff, then back at the warrior priests pursuing them.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: No! I'd rather get cut down than jump!

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Zip it.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hey! Wh—What are you doing?!
With the girl tucked snugly under his arm, Isidro takes one last look back.
Then he sets his sights firmly ahead and leaps down the cliff, a screaming Pascuala in tow.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: AHHHHHHHHH!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: You lousy piece of finshit, I'll remember this—!

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: AAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!
In the midst of her panic, Pascuala feels herself land on something soft, quite unlike the solid ground she expected.
As she opens her eyes, she sees the giant cloth used to catch her.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: We're safe now. They caught us with their sails.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Oh, there was... a boat... at the bottom of the cliff.
She looks around. Enormous bones prop up the ship's wooden hull, while layer upon layer of canvas and finleather sails throng the masts, scattering the sun's light.
The fiery wind powers the complex of legs at the bottom of the hull through a complicated transmission system, the legs sending the ship scuttling over the salty soil with their powerful strokes.

steps.name: 'Ordinary' Townsperson
steps.text: Still calling yourself a Master Thief after that courageous display, Pascuala?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Hah, a good thief acts with thorough planning and caution, not reckless derring-do.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Stop gabbing with her and get changed, Teach. The helmsman's injured and I need you to take over.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Didn't like that outfit anyway. Way too tight around the bodice.

steps.name: Menacing Sailor
steps.text: *Huff*... *Huff*...

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Hm? What's that you're carrying?

steps.name: Menacing Sailor
steps.text: Food and water!

steps.name: Menacing Sailor
steps.text: I spotted their granary earlier, so I snagged some in the chaos!

steps.name: Menacing Sailor
steps.text: Set it alight afore I left, too! Haha! They'll be too busy putting out the fire to worry about us.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Not half bad, you bastard.

steps.name: Teach
steps.text: Now put your backs into it, ladies and gents! We reach home tomorrow night!

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: What're you looking at, chaval? You'll fall over the railing like that. First time in Mar Pálido?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: This ship is... unusual. It's almost entirely wood and bone... Must be a lot lighter than the average landship.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Of course. Our salt ships are the only thing that can cross the Flat. If you tried it with those heavy iron beasts, they'd just get stuck in the salt.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Fascinating.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You don't look the least bit scared. Didn't you hear what the townsfolk called us?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Bandits.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You've got guts, saying it straight to my face.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I mean, you saved me from the gallows, didn't you?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Still, why run with us? The townies will brand you as one of us now.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Do you know of a sword technique that will let you cut through the sea's wind and waves?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: A sword technique? You having a laugh?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: So none of you know?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Never heard of it.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Where's your ship stopping?

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You want off? No can do, I'm afraid. You're heading back with us.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: ...Sorry, but that's not in my plans.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Not my problem, chaval.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Don't say that. I'd rather not have to draw my sword against the ones who saved me.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: I get that you're a dab hand with the blade, but...

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Grkh...

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You need to watch your back.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Heh, all these years as a thief, and not once has anyone spotted me as I make my move.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: That was enough dizzyleaf smoke to keep him asleep the entire trip.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Don't get cocky. So where's the compass the boss wanted? We put a lot of work into saving your sorry behinds, so don't disappoint us now.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: You wound me, señor. I've just delivered you more than just the compass.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: (Pouts) I got you my amigo over there too, didn't I?

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: In fact, considering the added value, saving me's not enough. I'll need a little something extra to make it worth my while.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: You think we're just gonna take your word for it that he's an alchemist? Wait til the boss checks him over afore you run your mouth again.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Fine by me. Whatever's meant to be in my pocket, will find its way there eventually.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Anyhow, where's the kitchen? I'm always a little peckish after staring death in the face.

steps.name: Javier
steps.text: Second floor of the stern.

steps.name: Pascuala
steps.text: Muchas gracias, O generous señor!

steps.name: Scared Warrior Priest
steps.text: AHHHHHHHHH!

steps.name: Scared Warrior Priest
steps.text: AAAAHHHHH—!

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: I'm only going to remove the bone spines from the wound, not amputate your leg.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Only the most vicious of bandits would make barbed blades like this... The bleeding's stopped.

steps.name: Scared Warrior Priest
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Hold on a little while longer. I've already sent someone to get Doctor Añora. Once she's here, we can have a better look.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Be at ease, you seem fine. You'll be better after a few square meals.

steps.name: Sad Warrior Priest
steps.text: Señor Calificador, we've put out the fire in the granary, but there's nothing left inside.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...I'll think of a way to feed us.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: What of the doctor? Her legs are not so good at her age. Did you not help her over?

steps.name: Sad Warrior Priest
steps.text: She's gone.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Then where is sh—Wait, what? What happened?!

steps.name: Sad Warrior Priest
steps.text: She was knocked over by the bandits and hit the back of her head. She is... no longer with us.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Scared Warrior Priest
steps.text: Señor Silver... Are you...?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Did that hurt...? Sorry... Bear with it.

steps.name: Anxious Townsperson
steps.text: She's giving birth, Silver! The widow's giving birth right now!

steps.name: Anxious Townsperson
steps.text: Might be because of the bandits' attack. Or not. Can we have the doctor see to her first?

steps.name: Anxious Townsperson
steps.text: ...Wait, where's the doctor?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Don't ask. I'll check on her myself.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Don't shake her. She won't be waking.

steps.name: Anxious Townsperson
steps.text: Señor, I... Señor, she... Señor, the child...

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: The child, too.

steps.name: Anxious Townsperson
steps.text: Señor, you...

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Clerics, guard the bodies. We bury them tomorrow morning.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: Sir.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Prepare a burdenbeast. After the funerals, go and search for Añora's son. We must ask him to return, no matter what.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: This town needs a doctor.

steps.name: Warrior Priest
steps.text: As I recall, she was teaching you some of her craft, was she not?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: A man who has only just learned how to make ointment cannot be considered a doctor.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Otherwise, the widow and her child would not have died.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Now go, back to work.
Through the tightly closed shutters of their windows, the people of Aarón can see a faint pink light floating through the fog-choked streets.
Silver does not know when it became dark. It feels like it was morning only minutes ago, when he was tidying up his robes for the execution.
But now, those robes are stained with blood. Not the blood of thieves or blasphemers, but of the townspeople.
Out of nowhere, he sees another faint pink light across the street.
A gaunt, lanky man with a bloody hole in his abdomen, large enough for him to see right through it.
The man calmly walks towards him, as if nothing was wrong.

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: Do you need assistance, señor?

steps.name: Silver
steps.text: You look gravely wounded.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I am fine, Señor Calificador. You on the other hand, look most pale indeed.

spans.text: on the other hand, look most pale indeed.

steps.name: Anastasio
steps.text: I am an alguacil, newly transferred. Might you require my assistance?

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: Ahh—

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: I must say, I didn't expect you to sleep so well hanging upside-down, joven.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: This sort of thing happens to me a lot. You get used to it.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Your old shed's as good as new. Remember to thank Javier. It took him all night to fill in that tunnel of yours.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: You could have saved him the effort if you just let me go.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Yet you're the one giving himself nothing but trouble by refusing to fix my compass. Do that, and you're free.

steps.name: Isidro
steps.text: I told you, I don't know a thing about alchemy. That's not going to change, no matter how many times you ask.

steps.name: Juana
steps.text: Send him back to his shed. And skip the bread for his meals.
